guide.summary: Forgejo documents OAuth2 for third-party apps that act with the user's consent, so OAuth fits a connected-person model. Each app is registered on the instance's admin applications page. The docs say tokens issued to OAuth apps carry administrative rights and that OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so a read-only boundary cannot be enforced by scope. No supplied source names a repository-listing endpoint, pagination parameters, or a repository-read grant. Set up and test on your own Forgejo test instance first. Hold the listing test's final mapping and customer rollout until those are documented.

findings.title: Apps are registered on each instance's admin applications page
findings.detail: OAuth2 applications are created on the instance-wide admin applications page. Each customer's own Forgejo instance needs its own app registration.

evidence.quote: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: OAuth apps receive administrative rights and scopes are not implemented
findings.detail: Tokens a user grants to a third-party OAuth app carry administrative rights, and OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented. Read-only access cannot be enforced by a documented OAuth scope.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.

findings.title: Personal and scoped access tokens are a different mechanism
findings.detail: Do not substitute a personal access token or scoped token for the OAuth2 flow. The docs state they are entirely different.

evidence.quote: Note Scoped tokens or personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2;

findings.title: Authorization and token exchange follow the documented flow
findings.detail: Send the user to the authorize endpoint with client ID, redirect URI, response type code and state. Exchange the returned code at the access token endpoint, using a redirect URI that matches the authorize request.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be
POST https://[YOUR-FORGEJO-URL]/login/oauth/access_token { "client_id" : "YOUR_CLIENT_ID" ,
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be
POST https://[YOUR-FORGEJO-URL]/login/oauth/access_token { "client_id" : "YOUR_CLIENT_ID" ,
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register a test OAuth2 app on your own Forgejo test instance
On your own test instance, where you are an instance administrator, create an OAuth2 application on the admin applications page. Record the instance base URL as an input and store the client ID, secret and redirect URI outside source control.
Fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL, CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, REDIRECT_URI

Implement the authorize URL, state check and code-to-token exchange
Build the authorize URL with client ID, redirect URI, response type code and state. Prepare the token request for the returned code. Do not run the exchange until consent completes.
Fields:

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Authorize the test account through the OAuth2 consent screen
Done when: The test account consents, is redirected with a code, and the code exchanges for an access token.

Obtain documented repository listing API
Done when: A documented repository listing endpoint, its required scope, version header, and pagination parameters are supplied in the provided documentation.

Inspect granted access and request log for read-only behavior
Done when: Granted access and the request log show only listing requests, and no create, edit or delete requests appear.
